name: Natural Language Processing
description: Processing and understanding text, from tokenisation and classical models to embeddings and transformers.

nodes.name: NLP tasks
nodes.desc: The main NLP tasks and why language is hard: ambiguity, context and variation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to name the main NLP tasks and explain why ambiguity, context and variation make language hard for computers.

nodes.name: Text preprocessing
nodes.desc: Tokenisation, normalisation, stemming, lemmatisation and stop words.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prepare raw text for models with tokenisation, normalisation, stemming, lemmatisation and stop word removal.

nodes.name: Regex for text
nodes.desc: Using regular expressions to clean, match and extract patterns from text.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use regular expressions to clean text and extract patterns such as dates, emails and numbers.

nodes.name: Corpora & annotation
nodes.desc: Text datasets, annotation schemes, inter-annotator agreement and data splits.
nodes.summary: You will understand how text datasets are built and annotated and be able to measure annotation quality and split data properly.

nodes.name: Bag of words & TF-IDF
nodes.desc: Representing documents as sparse count and TF-IDF vectors.
nodes.summary: You will be able to represent documents as sparse count and TF-IDF vectors and understand what these representations lose.

nodes.name: n-gram models
nodes.desc: Language models from counts, smoothing and perplexity.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build n-gram language models from counts, smooth them and evaluate them with perplexity.
topics: The chain rule and Markov assumption

nodes.name: Text classification
nodes.desc: Naive Bayes and logistic regression classifiers for topics, spam and sentiment.
nodes.summary: You will be able to train and compare naive Bayes and logistic regression classifiers for topic, spam and sentiment tasks.

nodes.name: POS tags & NER
nodes.desc: Part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition with HMMs and CRFs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to tag parts of speech and named entities with HMMs and CRFs and understand BIO encoding.
topics: Named entity types and BIO tagging

nodes.name: Sentiment classifier
nodes.desc: Build and evaluate a sentiment classifier for product or movie reviews.
nodes.summary: You will build and evaluate a sentiment classifier for product or movie reviews and analyse its errors.
topics: Evaluation with F1 and confusion matrix
Error analysis on negation and sarcasm

nodes.name: Word embeddings
nodes.desc: Dense word vectors with word2vec and GloVe and what their geometry captures.
nodes.summary: You will understand how word2vec and GloVe learn dense word vectors and what their geometry captures about meaning.

nodes.name: RNNs for text
nodes.desc: Recurrent networks and LSTMs for language modelling and sequence labelling.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply recurrent networks and LSTMs to language modelling and sequence labelling tasks.

nodes.name: Seq2seq & attention
nodes.desc: Encoder-decoder models and attention for translation and summarisation.
nodes.summary: You will understand encoder-decoder models and how attention improves translation and summarisation.

nodes.name: Syntactic parsing
nodes.desc: Constituency and dependency parsing and what parse trees are used for.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse sentence structure with constituency and dependency parsing and know where parse trees are useful.

nodes.name: BERT-style encoders
nodes.desc: Transformer encoders, masked language modelling and contextual embeddings.
nodes.summary: You will understand how transformer encoders like BERT are pretrained with masked language modelling to produce contextual embeddings.
topics: The CLS token and special tokens

nodes.name: Subword tokenisation
nodes.desc: BPE, WordPiece and SentencePiece and how they handle rare words.
nodes.summary: You will understand how BPE, WordPiece and SentencePiece split text into subwords to handle rare and unseen words.

nodes.name: Fine-tuning for NLP
nodes.desc: Adapting pretrained models to classification, tagging and span tasks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to fine-tune pretrained transformers for classification, token tagging and span extraction tasks.

nodes.name: NER with BERT
nodes.desc: Fine-tune a transformer to extract entities from domain text and measure F1.
nodes.summary: You will fine-tune a transformer to extract named entities from domain-specific text and measure entity-level F1.

nodes.name: Question answering
nodes.desc: Extractive and generative question answering over passages.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build extractive and generative question answering systems over passages of text.

nodes.name: Summarise & translate
nodes.desc: Sequence-to-sequence transformers for summarisation and machine translation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply sequence-to-sequence transformers to summarisation and machine translation and judge output quality.

nodes.name: Evaluating NLP
nodes.desc: Accuracy, F1, BLEU, ROUGE and human evaluation, and their limits.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose and interpret NLP metrics such as F1, BLEU and ROUGE and know when human evaluation is needed.

nodes.name: Semantic search
nodes.desc: Sentence embeddings for similarity search, clustering and deduplication.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use sentence embeddings to search, cluster and deduplicate text by meaning.
